prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: A few politicians were at enmity (1)/ with each other and no one was ready (2)/ to budge and this is what led to the division of the party. (3)/ No error (4)
options: A few politicians were at enmity
with each other and no one was ready
to budge and this is what led to the division of the party.
explanation: 'Each other' is used for two persons only; since 'a few politicians' means more than two, it should be 'at enmity with one another'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The five brothers (1)/ are at daggers drawn, (2)/ so they feel it below their dignity to talk to each other. (3)/ No Error (4)
options: so they feel it below their dignity to talk to each other.
explanation: With five brothers (more than two) the reciprocal pronoun must be 'one another', so 'talk to each other' should be 'talk to one another'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: He was so afraid (1)/ that his knees (2)/ knocked one another. (3)/ No Error (4)
explanation: Only two knees are involved, so the reciprocal pronoun for two applies: 'knocked each other'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: I am yet to come across two people who are (1)/ so bent on making one another's (2)/ life as miserable as they can. (3)/ No error (4)
options: I am yet to come across two people who are
so bent on making one another's
life as miserable as they can.
explanation: 'One another' is for more than two; with 'two people' it must be "each other's life".

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: But the other candidates were often so busy fighting with each other that, again he went unscathed.
explanation: 'The other candidates' refers to more than two persons, so 'fighting with each other' should be 'fighting with one another'.

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: We must / take care / of one other / in times of crisis.
explanation: 'One other' is not a reciprocal pronoun; the phrase should be 'of one another' (or 'of each other').

prompt: Identify the part with the grammatical error (or 'No error').
sentence: The two business partners frequently (A) / argued with one another over (B) / the allocation of corporate profits. (C) / No Error (D)
explanation: 'One another' is used for more than two; for exactly two partners, 'each other' is required. Correct: 'argued with each other over'.

prompt: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.
sentence: The three of them shouted out to each another when the train started moving.
explanation: For more than two persons the reciprocal pronoun is 'one another', and 'each another' is never correct.
